Interest 02 / 06

Investment

Where capital goes, and why.

Capital markets, portfolio construction, risk and return: the decisions that follow the analysis.

Three questions I start with

What does the company stand for? What is it worth? And what is it trading at? They are three different things, and the gap between the last two is where an investment case lives.

Focus areas

  • Equity research
  • Investment management
  • Portfolio construction and the Markowitz model
  • Private equity and venture capital
  • Risk management
  • Valuation
  • Capital allocation

How I invest

Long term, and through trustworthy mutual funds while my studies take most of my time. Price and worth are different things: I research like an analyst and invest like a busy student.

I treat research and investing as two different jobs. Research is where I practise judgement; investing is where I stay patient.

What I am studying now

CFA Level II is the main track, going deeper into valuation, derivatives and portfolio management. Alongside it I keep working through private equity and venture capital, derivatives and investment risk management.

Academic project

Portfolio Construction & Investment Analysis, built around Markowitz Modern Portfolio Theory. See Skills.

Jainam Broking Ltd.

Summer Intern · Equity Research

My most important internship so far: a summer inside the equity research function of a broking house, where the job is to turn company filings into an investment view.

The work centred on reading financial statements and annual reports, working out valuation and profitability measures, and writing company and industry research up in a form a client or portfolio manager can use. It is where the finance I had studied met a real research workflow.

  • Exposure to equity research and investment analysis within a broking environment
  • Financial statements and annual reports, read company by company
  • Valuation approaches such as DCF and comparable company analysis
  • Company and industry research across several sectors
  • Turning analysis into clear, structured written reports

Apr – May 2025 · Surat, Gujarat

Ckredence Wealth Management Pvt. Ltd.

Finance & PMS Intern

A structured internship in finance and Portfolio Management Services (PMS) at a Surat wealth-management firm. The internship certificate also credits hands-on work with NAV analysis, mutual fund classification, client onboarding (e-verification and KYC), SIPs, compliance paperwork, derivatives planning and ODIN software.

  • Account-opening documentation and KYC for individual, minor, HUF and other non-individual accounts; demat account structures, depository participants, plans and charges.
  • Assisted with client documentation (account records, ledgers, GST- and tax-related documents) and guided clients through selfie verification.
  • Equity trading: debit buying, pledging, associated charges and ageing, with exposure to ODIN trading software.
  • Options: terminology (ATM, ITM, OTM, spread), payoffs of long and short calls and puts, and the valuation and graphical representation of strategies.

Research & academic interests

Two research ideas, pinned to the board.

Note 01

AI Advisory vs Finance Influencers

Question How do retail investors compare AI-enabled financial advisory tools and finance influencers in terms of perceived credibility, trust, usefulness, and influence on investment decisions?

Proposed overview, not a completed study

AI Financial AdvisoryFinance InfluencersRetail InvestorsInvestor BehaviourFinancial LiteracyTrust and CredibilityInvestment Decision-Making
Open the note
Proposed abstract

This research explores how retail investors perceive two increasingly important sources of financial guidance: AI-enabled advisory tools and finance influencers operating through digital platforms.

The study aims to examine differences in perceived credibility, trust, accessibility, transparency, usefulness, and influence on investment-related decision-making. It also considers how investor characteristics and financial literacy may influence reliance on algorithmic recommendations compared with influencer-led financial information.

The research seeks to understand the factors shaping investor preferences and the implications of these emerging sources of financial information for responsible financial decision-making.

Note 02

Generative AI in Entrepreneurship

Question How does the adoption of generative AI influence entrepreneurial activities, including idea generation, business planning, productivity, and early-stage decision-making?

Proposed overview, not a completed study

Generative Artificial IntelligenceEntrepreneurshipAI AdoptionEntrepreneurial InnovationBusiness PlanningProductivityDecision-Making
Open the note
Proposed abstract

This research explores the role of generative artificial intelligence in entrepreneurial activities, particularly its potential to support idea generation, business planning, market research, content development, and early-stage business decisions.

It examines the perceived usefulness of generative AI in improving accessibility, productivity, and creative exploration while considering limitations such as output reliability, originality, data privacy, and over-reliance on automated systems.

The research aims to understand how generative AI can complement entrepreneurial judgement and support business development, while identifying the areas where human evaluation and verification remain essential.
